Grounded in Nielsen Norman Group (NN/g) Research: Behavioral Persona Archetypes • Verb-Driven User Need Statements • Self-Determination Theory
Core Human Domain: Volunteer Roster Management, Shift Deficit Resolution, Targeted Communication & Follow-up

div.div:
NN/g NEED STATEMENT FORMULA & PSYCHOLOGICAL PILLARS
Formula: [User/Persona] needs [verb-driven need] in order to [human goal/insight].
■ Autonomy: Choice, control, frictionless action | ■ Competence: Preparedness, mastery, verified proof
■ Relatedness: Warmth, community belonging, authentic human appreciation

div.div:
SARAH LIN • The Overwhelmed Grassroots Coordinator
Role: Project Coordinator (`ORG_MANAGER`) • Urban Harvest Food Pantry (Grassroots 501c3)
“I spend more time chasing unconfirmed volunteers on spreadsheets and sending individual text messages than I do actually running our food distribution.”
Context & Environment:
• Manages 8–10 shifts/week with 12–20 volunteers each across 2 physical warehouse sites.
• Works under high operational stress; understaffed shifts mean fresh food spoils or boxes go unpacked.
• Juggles a broken laptop at a desk and a mobile phone on wet, noisy staging docks.
Current Behaviors & Hacks:
• Maintains a color-coded Google Sheet that breaks when multi-edited.
• Sends BCC mass emails that get caught in spam filters; manually texts volunteers from personal cell phone.
• Scrambles Friday evening at 8 PM to send panic texts: 'Are you still coming tomorrow?'
Core Motivations (Self-Determination Theory):
• Autonomy: Reclaim operational control over staffing without working 70-hour manual weeks.
• Competence: Deliver reliable, 100% staffed community shifts with zero last-minute crises.
• Relatedness: Cultivate a warm, loyal core community of volunteers who feel seen and valued.
Frictions & Anxieties:
• Spreadsheet Blindness: Discovering a Saturday morning shift is only 30% filled at 9 PM on Friday.
• The 40% Ghosting Rate: Volunteers register weeks in advance, forget, and silently fail to show up.
• Post-Shift Exhaustion: Lack of time to send follow-up thank-yous, causing valuable volunteers to drift away.

div.div:
MARCUS VANCE • The Purpose-Driven Professional
Role: Community Volunteer (`VOLUNTEER`) • 32, UX Consultant • Volunteers 1–2 Saturdays/month
“I genuinely want to help my local neighborhood, but if I don't know where to park, what to wear, or who to look for, the anxiety makes me want to stay home.”
Context & Environment:
• Demanding corporate job during the week; volunteers on weekends to reconnect with purpose.
• Mobile-only lifestyle outside work hours; rarely checks personal desktop email on weekends.
• Values punctuality, clear expectations, and respect for his personal time.
Current Behaviors & Hacks:
• Signs up for shifts 2–3 weeks ahead, but searches his inbox 30 mins before departure for address details.
• Feels deeply guilty when personal conflicts arise, but hates making phone calls to cancel, leading to ghosting.
• Prefers direct text/SMS communications over bloated portal apps.
Core Motivations (Self-Determination Theory):
• Autonomy: Flexibility to pick convenient, impactful shifts and manage his commitments friction-free.
• Competence: Arrive on site knowing exactly what to do, what gear to bring, and how his effort helped.
• Relatedness: Experience tangible human connection with local organizers and fellow neighbors.
Frictions & Anxieties:
• Logistical Fog: Vague listings with no parking details, gate codes, or footwear requirements.
• Arrival Isolation: Showing up at an unfamiliar site and wandering around looking for someone in charge.
• The Recognition Void: Leaving after 4 hours of intense physical labor and never hearing a single word of follow-up.

div.div:
ELENA RODRIGUEZ • The Milestone & Credit Seeker
Role: Student Volunteer (`VOLUNTEER`) • 17, High School Senior • Needs 40 certified service hours
“I completed 16 hours last month, but the paper slip got soaked in the rain, and the coordinator hasn't replied to my emails to sign a new one.”
Context: Strictly smartphone-based (SMS, Instagram, TikTok); needs certified hours for graduation and scholarships.
Frictions: Paper verification sheets getting lost or ruined; coordinators taking weeks to sign verification letters.
Goal: Immediate, verifiable, tamper-proof digital proof of completed service hours.

div.div:
DAVID O'CONNOR • The Boots-on-the-Ground Field Lead
Role: Volunteer Site Captain (`ORG_MEMBER`) • Veteran Volunteer designated as site lead
“When 15 people arrive at a muddy park at 8:00 AM, I need to know in 10 seconds who is here and who has allergies—without clipboards in the rain.”
Context: Coordinates volunteers on site while Sarah manages the pantry warehouse.
Frictions: Illegible paper sign-in handwriting; not knowing if missing volunteers are running 10 mins late or ghosting.
Goal: 10-second mobile check-in and instantaneous headcount visibility in harsh field conditions.

THEME 1: SHIFT DEFICIT AUDIT & CAPACITY REVIEW
Operational Focus:
• Evaluating upcoming shift fill rates against minimum thresholds.
• Distinguishing critical role gaps (Lead, Driver) from general count.
• Detecting staffing risks 5–7 days in advance rather than night-before.

THEME 2: TARGETED DISPATCH & URGENT COMMUNICATION
Operational Focus:
• Reaching qualified, nearby candidate pools via SMS/Push.
• Frictionless 1-click slot claiming without password barriers.
• Preventing broadcast spam fatigue across the community.

THEME 3: PRE-SHIFT BRIEFING & RSVP CONFIRMATION
Operational Focus:
• Delivering actionable logistics (parking, attire, weather, lead contact).
• 2-way SMS RSVP (Confirm / Cancel) to mitigate ghosting.
• Automated waitlist promotion cascade upon early cancellation.

THEME 4: LIVE ON-SITE ATTENDANCE & FIELD VERIFICATION
Operational Focus:
• Rapid digital check-in (QR pass / PostGIS geofence).
• Real-time headcount reconciliation; late-arrival SMS ping.
• Replacing paper clipboards and manual roster tallies.

Operational Focus:
• Personalized appreciation message from coordinator within hours.
• Verifiable, tamper-proof digital service hours certificate.
• Micro-feedback and 1-tap booking loop for upcoming shifts.

NEED STATEMENT 1 (Sarah • Coordinator):
“Sarah needs to evaluate real-time shift capacity fill rates against minimum staffing thresholds days in advance in order to proactively identify critical service shortages before community operations are compromised.”
NN/g Insight: Focuses on the verb 'evaluate fill rates', not a dashboard widget. Satisfies Autonomy by granting proactive operational control.

“Sarah needs to distinguish between specialized role shortages (drivers, bilingual leads) and general headcount needs in order to target recruitment efforts toward specific qualifications rather than blasting generic requests.”
NN/g Insight: Focuses on 'distinguish role shortages'. Satisfies Competence by ensuring qualified role coverage.

“Sarah needs to broadcast high-urgency, contextual outreach across mobile channels (SMS/WhatsApp) to nearby qualified candidate pools in order to fill empty slots quickly without fatiguing her broader community with irrelevant blasts.”
NN/g Insight: Focuses on 'broadcast contextual outreach'. Eliminates spreadsheet phone tag; protects community goodwill.

“Marcus needs to claim an open shift slot or release an existing commitment with a single frictionless mobile tap in order to manage his civic schedule responsibly without guilt or cumbersome authentication barriers.”
NN/g Insight: Focuses on 'claim or release with single tap'. Removes cognitive friction; treats volunteer as an efficient human.

NN/g Insight: Focuses on 'receive arrival instructions'. Satisfies Competence and psychological safety; eliminates logistical fog.
